title: Stop Boiling Your Cabbage in Water. My Meat Market's $2 Pork Trick Makes It Taste Like Sunday Dinner
description:
🥬 Stop boiling your cabbage in a big pot of water. One cup of liquid, a lid and about two dollars of smoked pork make it taste like Sunday dinner. All 15 steps are written out below 👇

A man came into the meat market for one smoked ham hock. Two dollars and eleven cents. The next Saturday he came back and bought three more, because his wife said the cabbage tasted like her mother's. After forty-one years behind a small-town Iowa meat counter, Helen shows you exactly what she told him.

⭐ THE 15 CABBAGE TRICKS
1. Stop drowning it: one cup of liquid and a lid, 12 to 15 minutes
2. The two-dollar pork: bacon ends, salt pork or one smoked ham hock
3. Start the pork in a cold pan on medium heat
4. How you cut it: wedges for the pot, half-inch ribbons for the skillet
5. Picking the head: heavy for its size, like a bowling ball
6. The Sunday version: ham hock pot liquor, wedges on top
7. Lid on first, lid off at the end
8. Salt it last (smoked pork is already salty)
9. The little splash: 1 tbsp cider vinegar + 1/4 tsp sugar, heat off
10. Onion first, cabbage second
11. Save the hock: the meat for supper, the bone for beans
12. The smoked sausage version
13. Cabbage and noodles
14. Keep the drippings
15. Sunday dinner: wedges, pot liquor, crispy pork and cornbread

🍽️ THE SKILLET VERSION (about $4.60, 6 servings)
1 head of cabbage, about 3 lb, cut in half-inch ribbons
1/2 lb bacon ends, cooked slow in a cold pan
1 onion
1 cup of liquid, lid on 12-15 minutes, then lid off
A splash of vinegar and a pinch of sugar; salt only at the end, after you taste

🍖 THE SUNDAY VERSION
1 smoked ham hock, 6 cups of water, half an onion, a bay leaf
Lid on, low, about 1 1/2 hours
Keep about 4 cups of pot liquor, set the cabbage wedges in it
Pull the meat off the hock; freeze the bone for a pot of beans
